scope: Whole-commit orchestrator-level review covering NPC personality work, co-op hardening, save-state changes, world_renderer changes, and bridge-traversal test changes. Co-op-specific deep-dive lives in VS-050-local-coop-hardening-audit-2026-07-18.json.

findings.message: Big Five (OCEAN) personality traits + dynamic emotional state fields added with safe defaults (0.5 baseline, anxiety 0.1, irritability 0.2). Backward-compatible: existing NPCCharacter.new(...) callers get the defaults without code change. Hex-architecture compliant: pure RefCounted domain entity, no engine imports.

update_emotional_state(player_hp_ratio, player_score) mutates anxiety/happiness/irritability reactively with bounded clampf. Branches on agreeableness and role produce distinct friendly-vs-hostile reactions. Deterministic given inputs. Covered by test_npc_character_personality.gd and npc_personality_contract_test.gd.
degraded_for_combat_off() preserves personality traits AND dynamic emotional state in the copy. Correctly extends prior behavior (which copied only id/role/name/lines/visual).

_PERSONALITY_MAP hardcoded preset per known NPC id. Twelve NPCs covered (explorer, pirate, robot, coach, shopkeeper, banker, baker, merchant, farmer, scarecrow, parrot, mayor). Unknown ids fall back to neutral [0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5]. Application layer is the right home for presentation defaults; domain stays agnostic.
findings.risk: If a new NPC is added without a personality preset, it gets neutral defaults — silent but safe.

findings.message: _execute_npc_completions now calls active_npc.update_emotional_state(player_hp_ratio, _score) BEFORE building the LLM system prompt, then injects psych_context with the OCEAN + emotion snapshot. The NPC's response is therefore consistent with its current state. Prompt remains Polish-first; instructions now say 'dostosowując ton do swojego charakteru' (adapt tone to your character) instead of fixed 'przyjaźnie' (friendly).
findings.risk: Hostile NPC with high 'amused' happiness could produce a friendly-toned Polish response that contradicts its role. Bounded by the existing role instruction in the prompt.

findings.message: _PERSONALITY_MAP presets are author-chosen constants with no documented rationale (why is robot conscientiousness=1.0? why is scarecrow neuroticism=0.7?). Future drift risk: an author recalibrating one trait without understanding the design intent could break the per-NPC narrative contract.
findings.fix: Add a one-line comment per preset naming the design intent (e.g. '# robot: rigidly dutiful, no anxiety; scarecrow: lonely, anxious'). Optional.

findings.message: Three sites changed from `target.get_meta("resource_visual", null)` to `target.get_meta("resource_visual") if target.has_meta("resource_visual") else null`. This is a Godot-4 API compatibility fix — the two-arg variant of get_meta was deprecated. Behavior preserved.

_gather_world_resource previously emitted both 'inventory_changed' AND 'collect_<item>' to rules_runtime; now emits only 'collect_<item>'. The 'inventory_changed' event was removed without scanning rules fixtures for consumers. If any world rule or win-condition keys on 'inventory_changed', it will silently stop firing.
findings.verification: Ran `rg -n 'inventory_changed' data/ src/ tests/`. Confirmed `_commit_inventory` (gameplay_runtime.gd:1969-1976) already emits 'inventory_changed' when changed_item_id is non-empty. `_gather_world_resource` calls `_commit_inventory(inventory, item_id)` so the event still fires exactly once per gather. The removed direct emit was a DE-DUPLICATION fix, not a regression. `godot_rules_runtime_adapter.gd:72` checks for 'inventory_changed' and continues to receive it. Finding closed.

findings.message: Test coverage: defaults, dynamic emotion transitions for friendly vs hostile NPCs at low-HP and high-score regimes, and loader presets for explorer and pirate. Tests create fresh NPC instances per scenario to avoid state carryover. Headless-runnable.
Port-contract test integrated into run_contract_tests.gd. Verifies NPCCharacter field defaults, emotional state transitions, and loader preset binding for 'explorer'.

52 lines changed. Bridge rendering switches to Kenney Nature Kit centre/side/cap modules over the existing continuous walk surface (per PLAN.md 'Visual-route follow-up' entry). No regression to deterministic forest spawning or water mesh; test_world_renderer_toon_shader.gd and test_kenney_bridge_module_assets.gd cover the new contracts.

Bridge traversal test reworked: 76 lines changed. Walks every south/north ramp and deck checkpoint in both directions with a real CharacterBody3D. Exposed and fixed a rail-collider axis error that reached into the middle of the deck. Direct-play evidence is the live capture, not this test alone.

New 'Local-co-op control hardening' entry documents the P2 input isolation, single-undo semantic, and keypad 7/9 look-rotation. Entry correctly notes 'This is still one-screen local co-op, not a LAN or a P2P implementation; VS-051 owns the separate parent-authorized transport boundary.' Cross-references VS-051 accurately.

summary: Commit 1f2e571 is a mixed-purpose commit (NPC psychology + co-op hardening + bridge modules + save-state fix) that nonetheless hangs together: every change supports either the co-op sandbox slice or the governed-NPC direction. All twelve findings PASS at the implementation level. Two MINOR findings (personality-preset documentation, removed 'inventory_changed' rules-runtime event) and one LOW (PLAN.md entry accurate) are tracking items, not blockers. Co-op-specific deep-dive is in VS-050-local-coop-hardening-audit-2026-07-18.json. Hex-architecture boundaries preserved; no engine leaks into domain; new domain fields have safe defaults; new tests are headless-runnable.
approval_gate: Commit may stay on main. PLAN.md already documents the change. Backlog VS-050 evidence list should append this audit and the co-op audit JSON; VS-044 should append the Kenney bridge module test references.
